newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc has profit rise, sees growth.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc has profit rise, sees growth.

text.p: Chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc said on Thursday its 1996 net income rose by 28.4 percent to 2.740 billion francs ($494.9 million) and said it aimed to improve earnings further.
The results were in line with analysts' expectations.
Rhone proposed to increase its gross dividend to 5.25 francs per share, up 16.7 percent, and said its debt-to-equity ratio was down to 0.61 from 0.72 in 1995.

"In 1997, we will continue with (our) strategy and confirm our objective of achieving imporved performance in earnings per share and reducing the net debt-to-equity ratio to less than 0.5," chairman Jean-Rene Fourtou said in a statement.
Net earnings per share rose by 25.8 percent to 8.44 francs in 1996.

Rhone said the earnings per share had been reduced by 0.64 francs due to the recall of albumin products of the Centeon joint venture between its Rhone-Poulenc Rorer 68-percent owned drugs unit and Hoechst.
It said the rise in net income was esssentially due to earnings growth in pharmaceuticals and plant health activities, which represent 87 percent of earnings from operating income.
Sales were up by 1.2 percent to 85.818 billion francs.
Operating income rose to 6.892 billion from 6.223 billion.

"In 1996, we progressed in the implementation of our strategy. Our life science businesses continued to grow and improve their profitability, due to the commercial success of our new products and the integration of Fisons," Fourtou said.
"In chemicals and fibres there was a market improvement in the majority of businesses and new restructuring measures have been undertaken," he said.
"We have continued to refocus our business portfolio and in 1996 divested 6.8 billion francs of assets," Fourtou said.
The only earnings decline was at Fibres and Polymers, down by some 600 million francs to 326 million, which the company said was due to a worldwide polyester crisis. ($ = 5.536 French Francs)
